arxiv-2011-14213.title: HexGen and Hex2Spline: Polycube-based Hexahedral Mesh Generation and Spline Modeling for Isogeometric Analysis Applications in LS-DYNA
arxiv-2011-14213.creator: Yuxuan Yu, Xiaodong Wei, Angran Li, Jialei Ginny Liu, Jeffrey He and Yongjie Jessica Zhang
arxiv-2011-14213.description: Abstract In this paper, we present two software packages, HexGen and Hex2Spline, that seamlessly integrate geometry design with isogeometric analysis (IGA) in LS-DYNA. Given a boundary representation of a solid model, HexGen creates a hexahedral mesh by utilizing a semi-automatic polycube-based mesh generation method.

arxiv-2303-14466.description: Abstract Novel ”quasi two dimensional” typically layered (semi) metals offer a unique opportunity to control the density and even the topology of the electronic matter. arxiv-2305-03499.title: Adjoint and direct characteristic equations for two-dimensional compressible Euler flows.
arxiv-2305-03499.creator: Kevin Ancourt, Jacques Peter, Olivier Atinault
arxiv-2305-03499.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kevin Ancourt, Jacques Peter, Olivier Atinault. The method of characteristics is a classical method for gaining understanding in the solution of a partial differential equation. It has recently been applied to the adjoint equations of the 2D Euler equations and the first goal of this paper is to present a linear algebra analysis that greatly simplifies the discussion of the number of independant characteristic equations satisfied along a family of characteristic curves.

arxiv-2410-12724.creator: Haoyu Liu, Xin Sun, Pu Yu, Zijie Zhuang
arxiv-2410-12724.description: Abstract The conformal loop ensemble (CLE) is a conformally invariant random collection of loops. In the non-simple regime κ ′ ∈ ( 4 , 8 ) \kappa^{\prime}\in(4,8) , it describes the scaling limit of the critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn (FK) percolations. CLE percolations were introduced by Miller–Sheffield–Werner (2017).

pmc-10715943.title: From medical therapy to mechanical support: strategies for device selection and implantation techniques
pmc-10715943.creator: Letizia F Bertoldi, Andrea Montisci, Dirk Westermann, Mario Iannaccone, Vasileios Panoulas, Nikos Werner, Norman Mangner
pmc-10715943.description: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a complex clinical syndrome with a high risk of mortality. The recent, rapid development of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) has altered CS treatment. While catecholamines remain the cornerstone of CS therapy, tMCS usage has increased. According to shock severity, different treatment strategies including catecholamines alone, catecholamines and tMCS, or multiple tMCS might be used.

pmc-11529671.title: Evaluating the impact of transcranial electrical stimulation on post-stroke dysphagia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11529671.creator: Yanan Zhao, Zhicheng Zhang, Cuicui Wang, Hui Zhang, Ying Wang, Jing Bian
pmc-11529671.description: ObjectiveTo conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the impact of transcranial electrical stimulation (TES), proposed as a potential therapy for post-stroke dysphagia, on swallowing function in stroke survivors.MethodsThe PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases were searched for relevant studies on TES for post-stroke dysphagia.

pmc-12745140.title: Spinal cord–protective effect of resorcimoline for ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rabbit model
pmc-12745140.creator: Yu Kawahara, Takayuki Kawashima, Kenshi Yoshimura, Kazuki Mori, Ryotaro Nagashima, Tadashi Umeno, Haruto Nishida, Hiroki Sato, Akihiro Higuchi, Osamu Tokumaru, Shinji Miyamoto
pmc-12745140.description: ObjectivesSpinal cord injury can occur after aortic surgery as a result of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated during ischemia-reperfusion. Resorcimoline is a novel and potent antioxidant that has demonstrated ROS-scavenging activity in vitro. We evaluated the spinal cord–protective effects of resorcimoline and compared its efficacy with that of edaravone, a free-radical scavenger currently used clinically in Japan.

pmc-13050942.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of preventive training programs in reducing the incidence of knee injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13050942.creator: Hao Zhou, Yu-Mei Xing, Dong-Liang Zhou, Long Cui, Jia Qian, Jun-Nan Li, Yi-Feng Bu
pmc-13050942.description: IntroductionKnee injuries are highly prevalent among athletes. Following a knee injury, athletes may experience minor disruptions to their competition and training schedules, or in severe cases, the injury may even jeopardize their athletic careers. Incorporating targeted knee injury prevention training into routine training is thus critical for mitigating knee injury risk.

pmc-13226884.title: A dataset of orthogonal polygon-derived maze environments for path planning benchmarking
pmc-13226884.creator: Nguyen Kieu Linh
pmc-13226884.description: This paper presents a dataset of grid-based maze environments constructed from orthogonal polygonal structures. The orthogonal polygons are generated using a constructive generation framework. Building upon these polygonal structures, the present work further constructs maze environments by transforming polygons into grid-based representations, automatically generating start–goal configurations, and producing associated benchmarking data.

pmc-13419206.title: Dietary Supplements and Oxidative Stress Management in Young Adults Following Intensive Exercise: A Systematic Review
pmc-13419206.creator: Vlassios Kakouris, Maria Piagkou, George Triantafyllou, Karolina Akinosoglou
pmc-13419206.description: Strenuous exercise is a well-established physiological stimulus that enhances muscular strength and hypertrophy but can also increase reactive oxygen species production, leading to oxidative stress (OS). Numerous studies have investigated whether dietary supplements can attenuate exercise-induced OS, yet findings remain inconsistent, and methodological quality varies.

pmc-13566074.title: Public Perceptions and Determinants of Preference for Robotic-Assisted Surgery in the United Arab Emirates: Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13566074.creator: Yasir Ahmed Mohammed Elhadi, Aminu S Abdullahi, Abdelrahman Mohamed Alblooshi, Abdulla Alhosani, Arwa Al Khalidi, Mohammed Saleem, Shamma Rashed Mohammed Alrashdi, Reem Saleh Aljaberi, Azhar T Rahma
pmc-13566074.description: BackgroundRobotic-assisted surgery (RAS) is increasingly being integrated into surgical services worldwide. Successful implementation of robotic surgical technologies depends not only on clinical effectiveness but also on public trust, perceptions of safety, and willingness to use technology-enabled care. In the United Arab Emirates, the adoption of RAS is expanding rapidly; however, evidence regarding public perceptions and factors influencing acceptance remains limited.
